- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward sentiment spikes (sentiment < 0.2) — adjust downward bias to avoid premature recovery.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high or 1.2x prior close.
- Mean-reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is > 1.2x recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20%.
- Lagged sentiment influence: if sentiment drops sharply 3–5 days prior, reduce forecast slope downward.
- Avoid overconfidence in high-sentiment periods — if sentiment > 0.8 and forecast > 85% of prior 30-day high, cap at 85%.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment peaks and forecast rises, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter — if sentiment < 0.4, reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overestimating upside.
